_comment: The single definition of the branch policy. Every enforcement point reads
this file: the pre-commit and pre-push hooks, and the per-harness adapters
that enforce the primary-worktree rule (Claude Code, OpenCode, omp).
Identity is a git remote slug, never a filesystem path — a clone at a
different path is the same repo, and a path match cannot tell them apart.
Editing this file changes behaviour everywhere at once. That is the point.
_enforcement_active: Flip to true when core.hooksPath is set in dot_gitconfig.tmpl. While false,
the reachability and coverage checks skip with a reason rather than failing:
the hooks are installed but deliberately inactive, and a check that fails by
design every run is one nobody reads.
_enforced_surfaces: Agent surfaces expected to carry the rule-1 adapter. Add a surface here
when its adapter ships; the adapters-live check asserts exactly this list,
so an unshipped surface is not a standing failure and a shipped one cannot
_fail_mode: Accident prevention, not a security boundary. When the guard cannot tell
what a repo is, it allows and logs the reason: blocking on ambiguity
teaches agents to reach for --no-verify, which disables it everywhere.
A repo with no remote has nothing shared to protect and is unguarded.
